Command: Come, Take My Yoke, and Learn from Me
Summary: Jesus' invitation-command to the weary: come unto me, take my yoke upon you, and learn of me, for I am meek and lowly in heart.
Commandment: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart.
Application: Distinct from the repent-and-believe row as a discipleship word: the yoke is not removed but exchanged — his yoke is easy, his burden light — and learning happens under it, from a meek Master.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: 'ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light' (Matthew 11:29-30).
Function: Come — the invitation itself is the command. A New Testament command, not a Mosaic one — the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not sort it. Its goal was rest for the weary: take my yoke upon you, and learn of me, for I am meek and lowly in heart. The evil it addressed was the crushing yoke of self-chosen religion, labour without rest. It restrained that evil by exchange, not removal: his yoke is easy, his burden light, and learning happens under it from a meek Master.
